reviews.review:
I bought this game with some skepticism. What I saw didn't win me over much. But it was on sale and I thought "Hey, I need something to pass the time". So I bought the game.
And I found it to be a lot of fun. Found myself coming back to it every one day or two when I need a quick-play game.

But I have a major issue with the game. And that is:
[b]What good is a rogue game if you can't get past the second level?[/b]



Roguelike's are built on RNG areas/items/enemies, with the player trying to pass them, having a different run each time and dying a lot. That's what Roguelike's are. But there's also some balance needed for it. Bad RNG or Procedural designs lead to an [b]unbalanced[/b] game, NOT a challenging Roguelike.

Dying over and over on the first level is not justified just because it's a Roguelike. That's just bad balance/design.
The game is fun. Abilities are fun, Powerups are fun, even shooting and evading enemies is fun on its own!
But I've found some enemy and boss types to be just there to outright kill you.

There are different enemies with different abilities and behaviors. Some can be pushed back with bullets, others can't. Some charge at you while others stay afar and shoot. They're what make up the game. You can't just remove them out of the game cause the variety is what creates challenge and fun! Variety is the spice of life.

But there are some enemies that are designed intentionally to become Game Enders (or Run Enders if you may). Their behavior, their movement, their attacks all cause them to become hard to hit while easy to get hit by. These enemies just ruin the fun. Like even when you're fighting 15 enemies at once, you're still optimistic, saying that you'll beat these guys and go to the next stage. But then one of the aforementioned enemies drops by and you know that everything is ruined. You can't out maneuver him or kill him first with the horde behind you, so you just end up dying despite trying your best.

These enemies are what ruin the whole game for me. I like the shooting, the movement, the maps, the abilities, the powerups and everything, and I'm okay with dying over and over because of my mistakes or bad luck.
But I am NOT okay with dying to an enemy whose sole design purpose is to be a Run Ender. I find it cheap. A weak and cheap design. And it doesn't help that a third of the enemies are designed like this.

These enemies range from normal to bosses. I guess the easiest one to explain are the jellyfish.
As you can see in the trailer/gameplay videos, you can only shoot horizontally. Not even vertically like some old Sega games. This means that you always have to be on the same height level as your enemy to be able to shoot him with the exception being bigger sized enemies which give you more vertical hitbox.
So you can't aim anywhere but left and right and there aren't any staircases to level yourself with whatever you want.

Now in come's the Jellyfish. These are flying Jellyfishes which fly in from a screen corner and home-in on you. Pretty common for enemies, so what's the problem? They fly. They fly everywhere and they don't follow a movement like slowly become level with the player's height and then moving horizontally. No. These motherf*ckers can rotate in any direction they want. So when they fly from the top or bottom of the screen, they draw a straight line towards you and move towards you on that rail.
This means that they don't become level with you until they've actually reached you. So there is no way to hit them before they reach you. Maybe you get lucky and get a platform next to you, but you can only take 1 shot at them which is next to nothing.
They fly in, can't be hit until they are in your face, and since they are melee enemies, you're already stung when they reach you. And shooting them doesn't push them back. So you have to let go of EVERYTHING to make sure you don't get hit, which is not possible a lot of the times because they are not the only enemies in the map.


If these guys weren't bad enough, there's actually a giant Jellyfish boss too which is similar but with some new mechanisms, but are still as annoying as these little f*ckers. Considering how you have to kill a boss at the end of every stage, you're gonna meat this guy a lot. And since the game only has 3 bosses (at least for the first few stages) you're gonna see him 1/3 of the time.
Of the other 2/3, one is a giant slow enemy which is fine (the only okay boss I think), but the other is a Magma Worm which is even more annoying that the Jelly boss.

I'll break it down quick. He comes out of the ground with a small indicator (which is lost in the chaos or because of its size and color). The worm emerges from that point and if he hits you, he takes a big chunk out of your health. As he arches and gets  ready to go down, he homes-in on you. If he touches you again, you take damage again. How long is his cooldown before he emerges again? 2 second cooldown and around 2 second warning indicator. So 5 seconds maximum total.
Every 5 seconds this thing is gonna pop up. And since you're always in a fight, got a lot of visuals on the screen, and the indicator is small and its color can be lost in some enemies, you're gonna get hit by the f*cker a LOT!
How can you shoot him? You can only shoot him when he's emerging or going back down, because that's the only time it stretches and is low enough for you to him him. I'd say the window for each time is 1-1.5 seconds. So killing him is like grinding in a RPG game. It's gonna take a lot of time and no amount of skill can fix it.


I could go on about all the enemies with such horrible designs but I think you get the picture.



Overall I would not recommend the game.
Almost everything is fun, except the enemies. And since there's nothing else to do than kill enemies, everything is pushed aside and the whole game is dragged down because of a group of enemies with intentional bad designs. How do we know they're intentional? Game came out in 2013. If they were going to get fixed they would have been by now.
So yeah, I'd say that's a pretty cheap way to end a run. To design enemies out of the bunch to do just that.



No friend of mine was willing to buy this so I can't give any reviews on the Co-op. But remember this: You can't justify this game by saying "Yeah but you should play it with friends". This is not a Coop-first game like Left 4 Dead or GTFO. It's a Singleplayer with the option to play Co-op. So judging it on its Singleplayer is the actual way to do it.
Doing anything with friends is fun. Even poking needles at our balls is fun with friends, so any excuses regarding "you should play with friends" is bullsh*t.

Might have gotten one too many 56 leaf clovers.....

10/10 would recommend if you're looking for a challenge, and don't fear death.
its fun, if only i had friends for co-op :(

One of my favorite games. I put probably twice as much time offline on an old laptop. Although with too many items late game, it could really challenge that more mediocre computer. Overall, an excellent game.
